messages:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Multiple Route53 healthchecks flapping in eu-west-1b (azb). 50% failing, auto-page sent to #oncall. Links: https://internal.metrics/alerts/1925002345

alex: I'm on pager, looking. Can someone confirm if this is probe failures only or actual instance failures?

maya: I have the handoff in ~10m — leaving to devon if it's still active. Seen similar noise earlier but brief.

alex: quick check: probe agents in azb show "no heartbeat" for 3 hosts in the last 2m. Not showing instance terminations.

devon: joining call. pulled Route53 history, there are intermittent 503/504 responses to the healthcheck endpoint from the probe VMs. Running a curl now:

```
# from bastion-euw
curl -s -D - http://10.12.34.56/health || true
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Time-out\nConnection: close\n\n
```

monitoring-bot: Note: Telemetry ingestion shows a gap for azb probes between 1925002100-1925002250 (events dropped). Related alert: ingestion-backpressure-euw.

devon: ASG shows instances healthy, SG and NACL unchanged. No deploys. Could be upstream NAT gateway or AZ networking transient. I'll open a route53 failover to eu-west-1a for critical endpoints as mitigation.

alex: copying runbook snippet for route failover (runbook: https://go/runbooks/route53-failover)

```
# CLI to update weighted record set to prefer eu-west-1a temporarily
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.prod.internal","Type":"CNAME","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-1a","Weight":100}}]}'
```

ops-bot: Change recorded: route53-weighted-swap by alex (rollout window 30m). Change ID: CHG-7890.

product-support: We're seeing ~3 customer tickets with timeouts in eu-west that correlate with the alert window. Not widespread, but customers using streaming endpoints noticed disconnects.

noah: Flagging for priority: potential customer impact. If failover reduces errors, we'll keep it for 30m and then investigate root cause. Assigning postmortem owner: devon.

devon: Mitigation applied (rolled weight to eu-west-1a). Restarted probe-agent on two affected VMs (IDs i-0abc, i-0def).

monitoring-bot: Update: healthchecks recovered on 6/8 hosts in azb within 4m after probe-agent restart and failover changes. Some metrics still delayed (ingestion backlog). :white_check_mark:

maya: Handing off now — devon will be primary oncall. I'm OOO for the next hour.

devon: I'll keep watching and kick off a follow-up investigation into the ingestion pipeline backpressure that dropped probe events. Hypothesis: transient NAT gateway stall + ingestion backpressure suppressed probe telemetry, causing noisy Route53 signal.

alex: I'm updating the incident notes (https://docs.incidents/1925002345) with timeline and customer impact.

product-support: We'll send an interim customer status update saying we've mitigated and are investigating root cause; no data loss, degraded streaming for small subset.

noah: Please include rollback criteria and who approved the route53 change in the postmortem. Devon owns the follow-up and postmortem; alex will collect logs for the timeline.

devon: Ack. Will add logs, packet captures, and NAT gateway CloudWatch for the timeframe.

alex: Thanks team. Leaving monitoring hooks open for 60m. If any regression, re-escalate immediately.

monitoring-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Alerts suppressed for 15m to avoid chattering during backfill.

devon: Filing follow-up ticket: "azb probe noise due to telemetry ingestion suppression" and tagging network/sre/infra.

product-support: Scheduling customer follow-ups; will re-open if any new tickets.

noah: Great work — postmortem timeline and owner noted.

devon: signing off from active remediation, will run full RCA later today.
